requirement: The GSM-R network shall provide voice communication services for railway operations.
The GSM-R network shall provide data communication services for railway operations.
The GSM-R network shall support call-related services needed to establish, manage, and terminate communications.
The GSM-R network shall provide railway-specific communication services in addition to general telecommunications services.
The GSM-R network specification shall define a verifiable call set-up time requirement for the communication system.
The system shall support broadcast calls addressed to all members of a pre-defined group within a local geographical area.

During a broadcast call, the system shall permit voice transmission only from the call initiator and shall prevent all other group members from transmitting while allowing them to receive the call audio.
The cab radio shall provide radio communication capability through interfaces installed in the cab of a locomotive for principal use by the locomotive driver.
If the cab radio supports train control, the cab radio shall include the interfaces required to support train-control communications in addition to driver radio communications.
In direct mode, the system shall support back-to-back or set-to-set radio communication without use of ground infrastructure.

The driver alertness monitoring system shall monitor the alertness state of the driver and shall provide warnings and alarms to other systems when the monitored state indicates that such warnings or alarms are appropriate.
An EIRENE network shall be based on the ETSI GSM standard.
An EIRENE network shall comply with all mandatory requirements specified in the EIRENE FRS and SRS.
If an optional feature is included in an EIRENE network or EIRENE system, that feature shall be implemented as specified in the EIRENE FRS and SRS.

A group call function shall support communication to all members of a predefined group within a local geographical area, and during an active group call no more than one group member shall be permitted to talk at any instant while all other group members remain in listen-only mode.
The system shall support a group voice call in which the call initiator explicitly defines the set of participating parties before or at call setup.
For a group voice call, the system shall permit all participating parties to transmit and receive speech simultaneously without enforcing single-speaker turn taking.

The system shall provide a railway emergency call service with priority higher than non-emergency voice calls for informing drivers, controllers, and other concerned personnel of a danger condition requiring railway movements in a predefined area to stop.

The system shall support exactly two railway emergency call types: train emergency call for railway emergencies when shunting operations are not in progress, and shunting emergency call for railway emergencies when shunting operations are in progress.
The system shall provide each Secondary Controller with the ability to communicate with trains in all operating situations within the controller's designated area of track.

When a train is being pushed backwards toward buffers or any other potential obstruction, the radio system shall support a communication link from a designated lookout to the driver for reporting movement progress during the maneuver.
The radio system shall support ground-train voice communications and ground-train data communications for train operations.
The radio system shall support mobile voice and data communications for trackside workers, station staff, depot staff, and railway administrative and managerial personnel.
The radio system shall provide interoperable communications for trains and staff crossing national borders or other system borders between railway networks.

The radio system shall support functional addressing in which a stock number assigned permanently to an item of traction or rolling stock, and a train number assigned for a particular journey, may each be used as a component of a functional number for addressing users or systems.
On railway lines where international interoperability is required, the railway radio system shall comply with all requirements in this specification that are designated as Mandatory (M).
If an Optional (O) feature defined by the specification is implemented, the railway radio system shall implement that feature using the method defined in the SRS and FRS.
The railway radio system shall provide point-to-point voice call service, public emergency call service, broadcast voice call service, group voice call service, and multi-party voice call service.

The railway radio system shall provide a text message bearer service, a bearer service for general data applications, a bearer service for automatic fax, and a bearer service for train control applications.

The railway radio system shall provide the following call-related services: closed user group, multi-level priority and pre-emption, advanced call handling, auto answer service, barring of incoming or outgoing calls, call supervisory indications, and charging information.
The EIRENE mobile telephony system shall support functional addressing using at least one of the following identifiers: train number, engine number, coach number, or functional number.
The EIRENE mobile telephony system shall provide a shunting operations mode that emits or provides a link assurance signal while the mode is active.
The EIRENE mobile telephony system shall support railway operational emergency calls.
The EIRENE mobile telephony system shall support direct mode local set-to-set operation without requiring network infrastructure.
The EIRENE mobile telephony system shall provide seamless communication support for trains operating at speeds up to 500 km/h.

The EIRENE network shall support the following voice telephony service types: point-to-point voice calls, public emergency voice calls, broadcast voice calls, group voice calls, and multi-party voice calls.
Each supported voice call service shall be operable between any combination of fixed equipment users and mobile equipment users.
For each point-to-point voice call, the system shall provide full duplex communication such that both call parties can talk simultaneously during the call.

For each broadcast voice call, the system shall restrict speaking permission to the call initiator and shall restrict all other participating users to listen-only operation for the duration of the call.
For each multi-party voice call, the system shall support no more than six distinct participating parties and shall allow any participating parties to talk simultaneously.
The network shall support transmission of text messages from the ground to mobile users in both point-to-point and point-to-multipoint modes.
The network shall support receipt by the ground of text messages originated by mobile users.
If the text message facility is implemented, use of that facility shall not prevent any user from making or receiving a high-priority voice call or a high-priority data call.
The network shall support point-to-point data communications at a user data rate greater than or equal to 2.4 kbit/s.
If fax functionality is provided, an ongoing fax transmission shall be interruptible so that a user can make or receive a high-priority voice call or a high-priority data call.
The network shall support multiple call priority levels and shall permit an incoming or requested call with a higher assigned priority to pre-empt an active call with a lower assigned priority.
When a higher-priority call pre-empts an active lower-priority call, the network shall discontinue the lower-priority call and shall connect the higher-priority call instead.
The network shall restrict access to its functions and services to users contained in the allowed EIRENE user list, and shall deny access to any user not on that list.

The network shall support forwarding of an incoming call or data message addressed to one user to another user, and for voice calls the network shall allow the forwarding user to converse with the intended recipient before completing the forward.

The network shall allow a user to place an active call on hold, shall allow that user to re-join the held call at any later time, and shall notify a user already engaged in a call when another user attempts to contact them.

The EIRENE network shall support the following railway-specific services: functional addressing with registration and deregistration, location dependent addressing, shunting mode, and railway emergency calls.
The network shall support all EIRENE-compliant mobile devices.

For a radio installed in a vehicle with an external antenna, the network coverage shall meet the minimum signal criteria for at least 95% of the time over at least 95% of the designated coverage area.
The land-based part of the system shall provide communications for mobile devices when stationary and when travelling at speeds up to the lesser of the maximum allowable line speed and 500 km/h.

The network shall achieve end-to-end call set-up times of less than 2 s for railway emergency calls, less than 5 s for group calls between drivers in the same area, less than 5 s for operational mobile-to-fixed calls not otherwise covered, less than 7 s for operational fixed-to-mobile calls not otherwise covered, and less than 10 s for operational mobile-to-mobile and low-priority calls not otherwise covered.
The system shall achieve the required call set-up time in at least 95% of call set-up attempts.
For at least 99% of call set-up attempts, the observed call set-up time shall be no greater than 1.5 times the required call set-up time.
Any measured call set-up time used for compliance assessment shall include the time required to translate functional numbers internal to the EIRENE network.
When a railway emergency call is ongoing in a call area, any mobile configured to receive railway emergency calls that enters that call area shall automatically join the ongoing call.

When a call to all drivers in the same area is ongoing, any cab radio configured to receive that call type that enters the relevant area shall automatically join the ongoing call unless the cab radio is already engaged in a higher-priority call or in a call of equal priority.

The mobile radio subsystem shall provide three distinct mobile radio types: Cab radio for use by the train driver and/or on-train systems, General purpose radio for use by railway personnel, and Operational radio for use by railway personnel involved in train operations.
Each mobile radio type shall be operable in railway-allocated frequency bands around 900 MHz and in public GSM networks.
Mobile equipment shall function correctly while travelling at any speed from 0 km/h up to 500 km/h inclusive.

Each Cab radio, General purpose radio, and Operational radio shall support the following voice telephony services: point-to-point voice calls, public emergency voice calls, broadcast voice calls, and group voice calls.

Each Cab radio, General purpose radio, and Operational radio shall support the following mandatory call-related features: display of calling user identity, display of called user identity, and call waiting.
The EIRENE mobile equipment shall continue normal operation when exposed to pressure pulses caused by vehicles passing, entering, or leaving tunnels.
The EIRENE mobile equipment shall be capable of operation on board rolling stock.
The battery system used in the EIRENE mobile equipment shall provide sufficient capacity to support typical railway use for the intended deployment profile.

The design of the EIRENE mobile equipment shall comply with applicable European Norms for protection against physical hazards, including pollution, chemical contaminants, flammable substances, biologically active substances, dust, sand, heavy particles, and mould growth.
Stricter national environmental or physical protection requirements applied to EIRENE mobile equipment shall not prevent the use of other EIRENE mobile equipment within that country.
The Cab radio shall provide a Push-To-Talk function for use during group calls.
When a voice call has been established, the connected parties shall be able to communicate with each other.
When the handset is picked up during an active communication, the Cab radio shall transfer the communication to the handset and shall reduce the loudspeaker volume to its minimum level.
When the handset is replaced during an active communication, the Cab radio shall either cancel the call or transfer the call to the loudspeaker at the initial volume.
The Cab radio shall automatically handle calls with varying priorities.

The cab radio shall enable the driver to initiate a call to a page primary controller, secondary controller, or power supply controller with minimal driver action, with initiation achievable by a single keystroke when the destination identity is uniquely available.

After an appropriate controller destination has been obtained, the cab radio shall attempt to establish the call and shall present the called controller with the caller functional identity consisting of the train number if available, otherwise the engine number, otherwise the leading cab coach number.

During controller call establishment, the cab radio shall provide the driver with both an audible indication and a visual indication that the call is proceeding; if the call connects, the cab radio shall provide both an audible indication and a visual indication that the call is connected and shall connect the call audio to the loudspeaker at the pre-set value.

If a controller call cannot be connected, the cab radio shall provide the driver with both an audible indication and a visual indication that the call was not received by the controller, and the indication shall distinguish at least the cases where the called party is busy and where the network could not connect the call.

The cab radio shall support group voice calls among drivers within a pre-defined geographical area such that a driver can initiate the group call with minimal action, the participating cab radios display the group identity, the driver receives audible and visual call-progress indication, and once connected the call audio remains on the loudspeaker until the driver picks up the handset while speech transmission by the driver requires use of the handset Push-To-Talk control with a reminder indication provided.
The cab radio shall maintain an active group call until the call is terminated by the calling driver, an authorised controller, or the network.

If a train moves out of the applicable group call area or call area while a call is in progress, the cab radio shall leave or lose the call and shall provide the driver with both an audible indication and a visual indication of the loss of call.
If the cab radio is unable to connect a requested call, the cab radio shall provide the driver with both an audible indication and a visual indication of the connection failure.

When the Railway emergency function is activated, the cab radio shall provide a continuous visual indication in the cab and a short audible indication with duration between 0 seconds and 20 seconds, with 5 seconds used for trials; if the handset is off-hook, the audible indication shall sound from the loudspeaker at low volume and shall not sound from the handset.

If a train-borne recorder is connected to the cab radio, the cab radio shall send details of each Railway emergency function activation event, termination event, and failure event to the train-borne recorder when that event occurs.
When a cab becomes disconnected from an active multi-driver call, the cab radio shall provide a clear disconnection indication in that cab.
In each cab participating in a multi-driver call, the call audio shall be routed to the cab loudspeaker whenever the handset is on-hook.
If any part of a multi-driver call fails, the cab radio shall provide both an audible indication and a visual indication in each affected cab.

For a call between a controller and the lead cab, the cab radio shall support adding the controller to the active multi-driver call; if the controller initiates the call to the lead driver, the controller shall be added automatically to the multi-driver call, and the controller's functional identity shall be displayed in the leading cab.

Upon activation of the train-staff calling function, the cab radio shall present the driver with a selectable list of generic train-staff identities and, after the driver selects a target, shall establish a point-to-point voice call using the appropriate communication path determined automatically from the available onboard wire or radio systems.
When the Cab radio receives an incoming group or broadcast voice call, it shall provide both an audible indication and a visual indication of the incoming call to the driver.

When the Cab radio receives a group or broadcast call, it shall automatically connect the call audio to the loudspeaker if the handset is not in use, and shall automatically connect the call audio to the handset if the handset is off hook.

For an incoming broadcast call, the Cab radio shall display a visual indication on the driver MMI for the duration of the ongoing broadcast call, and the driver shall not be able to transmit speech into that call.

For a group call, the Cab radio shall permit the driver to speak only after the driver has lifted the handset, pressed the PTT button, and the network has granted permission; until permission is granted, driver speech transmission shall remain disabled. When the talk request outcome is determined, the Cab radio shall provide both an audible indication and a visual indication of whether the request was successful.

If a train-borne recorder is connected to the Cab radio and an incoming Railway emergency call is received, the Cab radio shall transmit the details of that incoming Railway emergency call to the train-borne recorder for recording, and shall generate an automatic confirmation at the end of the Railway emergency call.
The Cab radio system shall be capable of receiving incoming text messages.
The Cab radio shall provide a means to enter shunting mode and a means to leave shunting mode, and these functions shall be unavailable while any call involving the Cab radio is in progress.
When the Cab radio is in shunting mode, the system shall provide the link assurance tone through the loudspeaker.

If direct mode is implemented, the Cab radio shall provide a means to enter direct mode and a means to leave direct mode, and when the radio is in direct mode and normal network service returns, the user shall be given both an audible indication and a visual indication.

For communications using the Cab radio that do not involve the driver, the system shall indicate to the driver that the Cab radio is busy; for voice calls not involving the driver, the driver shall be able to listen to the audio output, join the communication by picking up the handset, and terminate an ongoing voice or data communication by selecting another call.
On Cab radio power-up, the Cab radio shall automatically perform self-testing, automatically select the pre-set loudspeaker volume, and initiate registration with other on-train systems.
On Cab radio power-up, the Cab radio shall attempt connection to an authorised mobile network and, where the last registered network is available, shall select that network for connection.

If connection to the authorised mobile network is successful, the Cab radio shall display the network name on the MMI and shall provide an audible indication of successful connection; if connection is not successful, the Cab radio shall provide both an audible indication and a visual indication of unsuccessful connection.
All failures detected during Cab radio self-tests performed on power-up shall be recorded in the train-borne recorder.
On Cab radio power-down, the Cab radio shall disconnect from the mobile network and shall retain any stored numbers present at the time the radio is switched off.
The Cab radio shall support presentation of radio-related prompts and information in at least 10 selectable languages.
At system turn-on, the Cab radio shall display radio-related prompts and information in the train-owner-selected default language stored within the system.

The Cab radio shall provide the user with a list of available languages and shall allow selection of the display language for radio-related prompts and information both at turn-on and during a journey.
When the handset is picked up, the Cab radio loudspeaker shall remain active and its output volume shall be reduced relative to the currently set loudspeaker volume.

The Cab radio shall block manual mobile radio network selection whenever any voice call involving the Cab radio is ongoing; otherwise, it shall allow the driver to view a prioritised list of all authorised mobile radio networks, manually select one using simple MMI actions, attempt attachment to the selected network, and upon successful completion display visual confirmation of the new network identity.
If automatic network selection is implemented, the cab radio shall provide the driver with controls to activate automatic network selection and to deactivate automatic network selection.
The cab radio shall not use automatic network selection for an international border crossing.

If directed network selection and/or automatic network selection is implemented, then whenever the cab radio changes to a new network without user intervention, the system shall inform the driver of the new network identity by both an audible indication and a visual indication.
When the driver is required to enter a train number manually, the system shall display the entered train number and shall require explicit driver confirmation before any further action is permitted.

If a train number is already registered on the same network and another train attempts to register the same train number, the system shall warn the newly registering driver by audible and visual indications, shall provide that driver with a means to override the currently registered train number, and shall inform the previously registered driver by audible and visual indications if the override occurs.

When a train number is registered, the Cab radio system shall automatically register the driver's functional number; when that train number is deregistered, the Cab radio system shall automatically deregister the driver's functional number.

If other on-train users are addressable through the Cab radio via the on-train bus, the Cab radio system shall automatically register or deregister each such user's functional number at the same time as registration or deregistration of the driver's functional number.

Where an on-train bus is connected to the Cab radio, the system shall support functional-number deregistration both on an individual-user basis and by a single driver-initiated action that deregisters all users, including the driver, when the train number is no longer associated with the train.

The system shall maintain a fixed association between each locomotive or coach stock number and the telephone number of the radio installed in that vehicle, and changing the physical radio unit shall not alter that association.

The Cab radio shall permit initiation of radio tests and, while any such test is in progress, the system shall continue to allow calls without being prevented by the test; upon test completion, the system shall display the test result in the same format used for the MMI power-on self-test.

The Cab radio shall support incoming and outgoing calls between the driver and on-train users or systems, including at least the conductor, public address system, and data systems, via appropriate interfaces and ports.
For data applications, the Cab radio shall permit call establishment and handling when the driver MMI is switched off.

The Cab radio shall provide a priority function that assigns and enforces different call priorities for calls originating from different sources so that contention for radio resources can be resolved.

When a higher-priority outgoing call request occurs during an established lower-priority call, the Cab radio shall give precedence to the higher-priority request by either placing the established call on hold or clearing it down (pre-empting it).

If run-time diagnostics are implemented, diagnostic tests on physical interfaces shall not interfere with normal operation of the Cab radio, and any detected interface failure shall be reported to the driver via the display.
The cab radio shall continue to operate for at least 1 hour after failure of the train power supply when subjected to a duty cycle of 20% point-to-point calls, 5% group calls, and 75% standby.
The driver man-machine interface of the cab radio shall include, at minimum, a display, a control panel, a loudspeaker, and a handset equipped with a Push-To-Talk button.
Radio equipment installed in a driver cab shall not obstruct the driver's vision or otherwise hinder the safe driving of the train.
All call-related functions of the cab radio shall be executable with the handset both on-hook and off-hook.
The emergency call button shall be red and shall incorporate protection against accidental activation.
When the driver safety device (DSD) is activated, the Cab radio shall automatically send a DSD data message without requiring manual operator action.
Each DSD alarm call/message sent by the Cab radio shall include the train number and the engine number.
The Cab radio shall transmit DSD alarm information to the primary controller.

The Cab radio shall provide a standardised interface capable of supplying the following event information to a train-borne recorder or other equipment: activation of the Cab radio emergency call button, receipt of an incoming Railway emergency call, termination of an outgoing or incoming Railway emergency call, transmission of a driver safety device alarm message, and details of confirmation of a Railway emergency call.
On-train mobile radio equipment shall provide a standardised interface to ERTMS/ETCS.
The General Purpose Radio shall support telephone operation such that an authorised user can initiate a call to any valid dialled number, subject only to call restrictions enforced by the network.

The General Purpose Radio shall permit transmission of a Railway emergency call only when that capability is enabled by a management function, and the call shall be initiated only through a special MMI action.
The General Purpose Radio shall reject any attempt to send a Railway emergency call by dialling a short code or telephone number.

Upon receipt of an incoming point-to-point voice call, the General Purpose Radio shall provide both an audible indication and a visual indication of the incoming call; where the calling party functional identity is available, the radio shall display that functional identity.

During an incoming group call, the General Purpose Radio shall prevent user speech transmission until the user has requested permission using the Push-To-Talk function and the network has granted that permission; the radio shall provide a visual reminder that Push-To-Talk is required and shall provide both audible and visual indication of whether the permission request succeeded.

Upon an attempt to connect to a mobile network, the radio shall provide a connection status indication such that: if the connection succeeds, the radio displays the connected network name and emits an audible confirmation; if the connection fails, the radio emits both an audible indication and a visual indication of failure.
After successful connection to the mobile network, the radio shall be capable of receiving all calls initiated using the radio's assigned telephone number or an appropriate group call number.

When the radio is switched off, it shall: terminate all calls under the control of the radio, disconnect from the network, clear the display, inhibit functions, and retain all settings and stored numbers present at the time of switch-off.

The radio shall support display of prompts and messages in at least 10 languages, shall allow the user to select a preferred display language, shall retain the selected language across power cycles, and on first power-on shall display the default language configured by the national railway.

Where more than one mobile radio network is available, the radio shall select the network automatically; when the radio changes network automatically, it shall provide both a visual indication and an audible indication; the user shall be able to override automatic network selection manually only when the radio is not in a call.
The General Purpose Radio, including its installed battery, shall have a total mass of no more than 250 g.
The General Purpose Radio shall allow a user to remove and replace the battery without the use of tools.
Replacing the battery in the General Purpose Radio shall not cause loss of user data or stored setup data retained in the radio.

The rechargeable battery of the General Purpose Radio shall provide at least 8 hours of operation from a single full charge when used on a duty cycle of 20% point-to-point calls, 5% group calls, and 75% standby.
When the remaining battery capacity is sufficient for only 10 minutes of full duplex call time, the General Purpose Radio shall provide both a visual indication and an audible indication to the user.
The Operational radio shall allow a user to initiate a call to any valid telephone number, while preventing calls that are restricted by the network.

The Operational radio shall provide the user with a means to establish a call to each supported controller type: primary controller, secondary controller, and, where implemented, power supply controller.

When more than one valid number is stored for a controller type, the radio shall present the identities of the available controllers with both audible and visual prompting, permit the user to select one identity, use the selected controller number for the call attempt, and abandon the call attempt if no selection is made within 10 seconds.

After obtaining an appropriate controller number, the radio shall attempt to establish the call using railway operation priority and shall provide the user with both audible and visual indication while the call is proceeding, when the call is connected, and when the system is unable to connect the call.
The radio shall allow initiation of a Railway emergency call by operation of a single red button.

When the operational radio is switched on and the emergency button is not pushed, the radio shall provide both an audible indication and a visual indication upon receipt of an incoming point-to-point voice call.

When the operational radio receives an incoming group or broadcast voice call, the radio shall provide a short audible indication and a visual indication of the incoming call, and shall display the group identity for a voice group call.
For an incoming broadcast voice call, the radio shall inform the user that speaking is not permitted as part of the broadcast call.

For an incoming group call, the radio shall require the user to request permission to speak by using the Push-To-Talk function, shall provide a visual reminder that Push-To-Talk is required, and shall prevent the user from speaking until permission is granted by the network.

If shunting mode is implemented, the radio shall provide a means to enter and leave shunting mode, shall disable entry to and exit from shunting mode while any call involving the operational radio is ongoing, and shall provide the link assurance tone via the loudspeaker while in shunting mode.
If connection to a mobile network is successful, the radio shall display the name of the connected network and shall provide an audible confirmation of successful connection.
If connection to a mobile network is not successful, the radio shall provide both a visual indication and an audible indication of the unsuccessful connection.
When switched off, the radio shall terminate all calls initiated by the radio, disconnect from the network, clear the display, and inhibit functions.
When switched off, the radio shall retain all settings and stored numbers that were stored at the time of switch-off.

The radio shall support display of prompts and messages in at least 10 languages, shall allow the user to select a preferred display language, shall retain the selected language setting, and, on first power-on, shall display the default language set by the national railway.

The Operational radio shall continue to operate as specified after exposure to the following environmental conditions encountered on the operational railway: salt mist spray, torrential rain up to 2 mm/min, heavy hail, snow storms, sand storms, accretion of ice, and corrosive atmospheres including sulphur dioxide, hydrogen sulphide, nitrogen oxides, ozone, and organic hydrocarbons.
The Operational radio controls shall be operable by a user wearing gloves.
The Operational radio including its battery shall have a total mass not greater than 800 g.
Battery replacement shall be possible without tools and shall not cause loss of data stored in the Operational radio.

The Operational radio shall use a rechargeable battery that provides at least 8 hours of operation from a single full charge when used with a duty cycle of 20% point-to-point calls, 60% group calls, and 20% standby.
The controller equipment shall provide a visual indication to the user whenever network service is no longer available.
The controller equipment should provide an audible indication to the user whenever network service is no longer available.
The primary controller MMI should queue all incoming calls and call requests.

The primary controller MMI should display the incoming-call queue to the controller, including each caller's functional identity and priority, and shall present high-priority calls at the top of the queue.
The primary controller MMI should allow the controller to select any currently queued incoming call for handling.
The EIRENE system shall enable each user to originate calls using a functional number and to receive calls addressed to that functional number.
The system shall assign each mobile exactly one telephone number that is unique across all mobiles in the EIRENE network.
The system shall assign each on-train function a unique standard number such that no two distinct on-train functions share the same standard number.

The system shall represent every maintenance team number as the association of exactly these components: service area identifier, maintenance team type (speciality code), and maintenance team identifier.
The system shall provide configuration controls that allow each railway network to define and modify group call service areas within that network's operational responsibility.
The EIRENE network shall support standardized UIC group numbering for group calls across fixed railway networks within the EIRENE network.
In a network boundary area, the EIRENE network shall allocate the pre-defined local area on a bilateral basis between the affected networks.
The EIRENE network shall permit authorized EIRENE users to receive calls initiated by calling parties outside the EIRENE network.

The EIRENE network shall implement exactly five call priority levels: Railway emergency; Control-command (safety); Public emergency and group calls between drivers in the same area; Railway operation; Railway information.
When a call requires pre-emption, the EIRENE network shall pre-empt the lowest-priority ongoing call before any higher-priority ongoing call.
The system shall support per-mobile activation and deactivation of each subscribed group membership.
When a group is activated on a mobile, the system shall permit the user of that mobile to receive calls addressed to that group.
When a group is deactivated on a mobile, the system shall prevent the user of that mobile from receiving calls addressed to that group.
For any mobile with a Railway emergency group call subscription that is operational, the system shall prevent deactivation of the Railway emergency group subscription.

The system shall order authorised network selection with highest preference to the home EIRENE network, next preference to foreign EIRENE networks, and lowest preference to public networks; if automatic selection is enabled, the system shall automatically select using this order.

The system shall provide a functional addressing capability that allows communications to be addressed to a functional number representing a user's functional role instead of the telephone number or terminal equipment identifier currently used by that user.
The system shall allow a single EIRENE user to have at least 3 functional numbers assigned concurrently.
The system shall enforce that no more than one EIRENE user is assigned to the same functional number at any given time.

The system shall permit a user to activate a functional number while connected through one network and later cancel that same functional number while connected through a different network, without requiring reassignment of the number.

The system shall preserve the validity and reachability of an assigned functional number while the associated user roams between networks, and this behavior shall be independent of the specific mobile or terminal equipment configuration used to access the network.

The system shall ensure that every functional number is unique across all supported networks, including public-network implementations of EIRENE facilities, and shall reject any registration or assignment that would create a duplicate functional number.
The system shall restrict each functional number to numeric characters only.

For each call, the system shall present the called user's functional identity to the call initiator and shall present the initiator's functional identity to the receiving user; for broadcast or group voice communications, the presented functional identity shall be the broadcast or group identity.

Before call establishment, if the initiating user has more than one functional identity available, the system shall provide a means for the user to select which functional identity will be presented to the receiving user.

All EIRENE user equipment shall support registration of functional numbers, and the system shall allow registration of up to ten functional numbers for items of equipment physically connected to the Cab radio within 30 seconds while preventing mis-allocation and duplicate registrations.

Following a system failure that causes loss of functional addressing facilities, the system shall provide a recovery procedure that restores the data set to a consistent state before functional addressing is returned to service.

During any recovery period after a system failure in which functional addressing facilities are lost, the system shall reject any attempt to use a functional number until that functional number has been verified.
The system shall support deregistration of up to 10 functional numbers assigned to equipment physically connected to the cab radio within 30 seconds of initiation of the deregistration procedure.
Upon successful deregistration of a functional number, an EIRENE mobile shall remove that functional number from the display and shall provide a user indication that deregistration has taken place.

After selection of a new network, the system shall automatically re-register previously registered functional numbers without manual intervention and, upon completion of re-registration, shall display the new registration details to the user.
The EIRENE text messaging service shall support transfer of text messages between ground systems and mobile radios in both directions.
Each text message segment transmitted through the EIRENE system shall contain no more than 96 characters.
For at least 95% of transmitted text message segments, the end-to-end transfer time for each segment shall be less than 30 seconds.
Use of the text messaging facility shall not prevent or degrade a user's ability to use the radio for its primary communication functions.
The mobile radio shall provide a standard data interface to connect the application module used for text messaging.

The radio system shall determine the Railway emergency call type automatically from the mobile's current mode of operation such that, if the mobile is in shunting mode, activation of the emergency call button initiates a Shunting emergency call, and otherwise initiates a Train emergency call.
When a Train emergency call is initiated, the system shall send the call to all drivers and controller(s) within the pre-defined emergency-call area associated with the initiating mobile.

When a Shunting emergency call is initiated, the system shall send the call to all users involved in shunting operations in the shunting area, and the Shunting emergency call shall automatically take priority over the link assurance signal.

The system shall allow initiation of a Railway emergency call by a simple MMI action and shall establish a Railway-emergency-priority connection to the pre-determined set of receiving mobiles and controller(s). If the connection is not established, the system shall automatically retry for 30 seconds.

During the 30-second emergency-call connection retry period, the system shall provide the originating user with audible and visual indications that connection is being attempted; if the connection is still unsuccessful after 30 seconds, the system shall provide an audible and visual indication that connection failed. Upon emergency-function activation, the system shall provide audible indication for 5 seconds and continuous visual indication at the originating terminal and all receiving terminals; terminals entering the affected area after completion of the warning stage shall receive the same audible and visual indications.
The system shall ensure that any information transmitted during a Railway emergency call after the warning tone is delivered only to the same set of users that received the warning tone.

The system shall permit termination of a Railway emergency call only by one of the following: the call originator, a controller participating in the call, or the network after a nationally determined period with no speech.

If a radio moves out of the call area while a Railway emergency call is in progress, the system shall provide the user with both an audible indication and a visual indication that the call has been lost.
An authorised EIRENE mobile shall be capable of receiving a Railway emergency call at any time while the mobile is powered up.

The system shall automatically generate a Railway emergency call confirmation message without user input, starting at the end of the call or when the radio moves out of the call area; if network contact is unavailable at that time, the system shall start the confirmation mechanism as soon as communications are regained, but shall not defer successful contact attempts beyond 5 minutes.
The system shall ensure that a confirmation message is received at the central location with a probability of success of at least 99% within 5 minutes after call termination.
The confirmation procedure shall operate independently of the mobile's current usage state and shall not cause network overload.
When shunting mode is active, the system shall establish shunting calls as group calls with priority set to 'Railway operation'.

During an active shunting group call and except while a link assurance signal is being transmitted, any member of the shunting group shall be able to use the PTT function to speak to all other members of the group.

During transmission of a link assurance signal, the system shall allow only the originator of that link assurance signal to use the PTT function to speak to all other members, and the system shall permit at most one shunting group member to transmit a link assurance signal at any given time.
The system shall permit any active member of a shunting group, including the driver, to initiate a shunting emergency call that is transmitted to all shunting groups within the area of coverage.
The system shall permit all shunting drivers and shunting group members to receive a shunting emergency call from any equipment that is capable of participating in shunting communications.
Upon reception of a shunting emergency call, the system shall interrupt any audible link assurance signal currently being output by the receiving equipment.

If a user who is an active member of a shunting group and is not the shunting leader attempts to initiate another call while the shunting communication is ongoing, the system shall ignore the call attempt and shall not establish the additional call.
If the radio used by the shunting leader to initiate a shunting group call is switched off, the system shall terminate that shunting group call.

The radio system shall generate a link assurance signal for shunting communications as an intermittent audio tone with a frequency between 800 Hz and 850 Hz, where each tone burst lasts 1 second followed by a 2 second silent interval.
Upon receipt of a shunting emergency call, the radio system shall deactivate the link assurance signal.

During transmission of the link assurance signal, every member of the shunting group except the signal initiator shall be prevented from speaking, while still being permitted to initiate a shunting emergency call at any time.

Operational radios used for shunting shall support a maintenance-selectable operating mode in which, when the initiator presses PTT to speak, the link assurance signal is either interrupted without being cancelled (Mode A) or remains uninterrupted (Mode B).
Within a given area, a radio set shall be capable of operating in any shunting group active in that area, subject only to applicable user access restrictions.
If direct mode is implemented, the system shall provide direct-mode voice communication with an operational range of at least 2000 m between a transmitter and receiver in open terrain.

If direct mode is implemented, the system shall provide voice-only communication in open-channel mode such that every user operating in direct mode and within radio range of the transmitting user receives the transmission.

If direct mode is implemented, the system shall support half-duplex operation such that a user can either talk or listen, but not both simultaneously, and transmission shall be initiated using a Push-To-Talk control.

If direct mode is implemented, at least one direct-mode channel shall be available; if more than one direct-mode channel is provided, the equipment shall provide a user function for manual channel selection.

For equipment that provides both normal mobile telephony and direct mode, the equipment shall permit selection of direct mode only when normal mobile telephony service is unavailable, shall allow switching between the two modes in a manner resistant to accidental activation, and when direct mode is being used as a fall-back shall provide both audible and visual indication when normal mobile telephony service returns.
